A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison after matching renumbered and relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original human detection, prompt-refinement, automatic detection, and preference results, including detection accuracy over 8,778 instances in Table 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results, including human detection scores, prompting evaluations, annotator agreement, and preference distributions.

M1.justification: The expert-guided prompt refinement and generation procedures are retained. Appendix E and Table 8 contain the same original and improved prompts; rewritten explanations do not introduce method components.

E1.justification: The 16 datasets, nine languages, nine domains, and tasks are retained. Appendix D.7 revises the reported Kazakh evaluator population from two native speakers to one native speaker and one proficient speaker. This changes the population description without establishing new recruitment or a rerun.

E2.justification: The evaluated generator comparisons, including Anita, Llama3-405B, and GPT-4o for Italian, remain unchanged. Both versions also evaluate the same 26 automatic detection approaches. Newly cited work does not add evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The four detection procedures, zero/few-shot conditions, sample counts, generation settings, and accuracy metric are retained. The setting identifiers are reassigned, but matching their names and task descriptions establishes no procedural change.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same prompt-refinement analyses, language-specific detection cues, case examples, preference analyses, and three-annotator assessment of 200 Chinese essays. Relocated figures and expanded interpretations add no new analysis.

E5.justification: Annotator averaging and the agreement assessment in Appendix E.10 are retained. No new repeated runs, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimation procedures appear. The revised recommendation to involve more annotators concerns future work.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their results, including 87.6% original human detection accuracy, 72.5% after prompt refinement, and lower accuracy for 19 of 26 automatic detectors. Arabic dialect scores change only from two-decimal to one-decimal presentation. Preference counts and appendix findings are retained.

T1.justification: The symbolic human/machine text descriptions and four task formulations remain equivalent after matching setting names. Neither version introduces theoretical results, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: experts can achieve high detection accuracy, prompting partly bridges distinguishable gaps, and human-written text is not always preferred. The multilingual study scope and released-resource contribution are retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds an explicit rationale that single-text detection should be hardest because it lacks comparison references. Section 3.2 adds dialect diversity as a source of difficulty and removes the explicit Wikipedia-memorization explanation. Appendix G.1 expands interpretation of human emotional advice using existing examples.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit dataset access link in the abstract, whereas v2 states that resources are released without that link. It also documents annotator qualifications more precisely through degree information in Table 3 and counts and research experience in Section 2.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds Russell et al. on experienced human detectors, Su et al. and Ta et al. on mixed authorship, and Pedrotti et al. on style-based detector evasion. Elangovan et al., OUTFOX, and MAGE gain references elsewhere. These extend context without substantially redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v3 revises prose in the setup, ethics, related work, and several appendix descriptions; adjusts Section 2 subheadings and setting identifiers; and updates author information and acknowledgments. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All nine tables and six numbered figures are retained. Tables 1–3 are reformatted, with annotator qualifications added to Table 3. The Arabic dialect table moves from appendix Table 6 to main-text Table 4, and automatic detection Figure 6 becomes main-text Figure 3. Other displays are repositioned or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 provides concrete dataset access information, more precise annotator qualifications, and relevant additional research context. Reformatted and relocated comparisons improve accessibility while retaining the empirical evidence. These are limited gains, partly offset by appendix setting identifiers that were not updated to match the main-text renumbering.
